policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 18 Feb close (1x4 3.72, 3x6 3.51, 6x9 3.36, 9x12 3.33 vs WIBOR 3M 3.85) price roughly 50bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The MPC held at 4.00% on 4 Feb; the statement says CPI may fall in Q1 and stay consistent with the target in coming quarters. Glapiński (5 Feb): a March cut if the projection shows nothing worrying; 3.5% possible as the end-point. Most MPC members now point to a 25bp cut in March (Kotecki, Masłowska, Zarzecki, Wnorowski); Litwiniuk floated 50bp in April instead. Dąbrowski (18 Feb): April safer than March, 50% odds for March.
policy.risk_text: January CPI (2.2%) beat forecasts before the basket revision; if the March projection disappoints, the cut slips to April (Dąbrowski) and the front end backs up; oil spikes on Iran and US tariff changes move the long end.

cpi.m: Jan flash (GUS, 13 Feb; 2025 weights, revision mid-March); Dec 2.4%

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); the March 2026 projection comes with the 3-4 Mar MPC.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~7.0% of GDP; 2026 budget deficit cap PLN 271.7bn (in force; at the Constitutional Tribunal for follow-up review), gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn; the Sejm passed the SAFE defence-loan law (13 Feb), and SAFE loans sit outside the Polish public-debt definition (MoF); January central-budget deficit PLN 3.7bn (1.4% of the limit).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~36% (18 Feb) financed; budget accounts PLN 183bn at end-January; Fitch reviews Poland on 27 Feb (after the close) and Moody's on 20 Mar, both with negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 4.00% on 14 Jan and 4 Feb; January flash CPI 2.2% y/y (13 Feb; 1.9% expected); 2025 GDP grew 3.6% (30 Jan); Q4 +4.0% y/y (12 Feb). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 18 Feb: the MoF auction sold PLN 13.0bn (demand 22.1bn) plus 2.1bn additional; ~36% of 2026 needs financed; the 10Y broke below 5% (ING); Dąbrowski called April safer than March (50% odds for March). Abroad: FOMC minutes read hawkish (several open to two-way guidance); UK CPI 3.0%; Brent +4.3% on reports that US-Iran war was close.

calendar.plan_text: MoF February plan (30 Jan): sale auctions on 11, 18 and 25 Feb (PLN 7-12bn each), no switch auction, a 33-week T-bill auction on 6 Feb; January sales were ~PLN 41.6bn incl. additional sales. BGK placed PLN 1bn of FWA0931 (Armed Forces Support Fund) privately (29-30 Jan). JPY 211.6bn priced on 6 Feb (3Y 1.88%, 5Y 2.22%, 10Y 2.90%, 20Y 3.65%); 33-week T-bills PLN 2.6bn at 3.529%. 11 Feb: PLN 11.9bn sold vs 25.8bn demand (cover 2.18) plus 1.38bn additional; OK0128 unsold; stop yields PS0131 4.298%, DS1033 4.732%, DS1035 5.035%, WS0437 5.148%. 18 Feb: PLN 13.0bn vs 22.1bn (cover 1.70) plus 2.12bn; stop yields OK0128 3.400%, PS0730 4.101%, PS0131 4.212%, DS1034 4.792%, DS1035 4.927%.
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug 2025-Feb 2026 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (25 Feb). February covers so far: 2.18x (11 Feb), 1.70x (18 Feb). The 3-4 Mar MPC with the new projection is the next event; a 25bp cut is the consensus.

core_text: Regime: the NBP paused at 4.00% with ~50bp more priced, the ECB is on hold at 2.00%, the Fed holds into June, the BoE eases gradually, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 55bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 221bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 18 Feb close). Hawkish FOMC minutes and an Iran-driven oil spike (18 Feb).
